title: Article 370: Dr. Ambedkar's Principled Refusal
summary: When asked to draft special autonomous provisions for Jammu & Kashmir, Ambedkar refused: 'You wish India to defend your borders and feed your people, but deny Indian citizens equal rights in Kashmir. I cannot consent to such injustice.'
full_text:
In late 1949, Kashmiri leader Sheikh Abdullah arrived in New Delhi with a missive from Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru, requesting Law Minister Dr. B. R. Ambedkar to draft a special constitutional clause granting exceptional autonomy to Jammu & Kashmir.

Sheikh Abdullah entered Ambedkar's office and presented the proposed draft.

Ambedkar scrutinized the text line by line. His gaze grew stern. Looking up, he fixed Sheikh Abdullah with an unyielding stare:

"Mr. Abdullah! Examine what you are demanding from the Indian Republic:
You expect the Indian armed forces to defend your territory from external invasion;
You demand that the Indian treasury allocate billions of rupees to construct your highways and infrastructure;
You expect Indian citizens to supply subsidized food grains to your state!

Yet, in return... you demand that the Indian Parliament shall possess no legislative jurisdiction over Kashmir!
You demand that citizens from other Indian states shall possess no right to acquire property or enjoy equal fundamental rights in Kashmir!
Do you genuinely expect me to draft such a one-sided, unequal covenant?"

Sheikh Abdullah replied uncomfortably: "The unique political circumstances of Kashmir necessitate special provisions, Doctor."

Ambedkar slapped the draft onto his desk and delivered his uncompromising verdict:
"Mr. Abdullah! I am the Law Minister of India!
I will not commit treason against the sovereign equality of the Indian people!
A covenant that demands all rights from the Union while denying reciprocal equality to the citizens of that Union will never be penned by this hand!
If the Prime Minister desires this provision, he must find someone else to draft it!"

Ambedkar dismissed the meeting.

Because Ambedkar refused to draft the clause, Nehru was forced to entrust the assignment to N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.

Ambedkar demonstrated that true constitutional patriotism requires absolute reciprocity and equal rights for every citizen under the national canopy.
moral: Constitutional covenants must balance rights with responsibilities; asymmetric privileges undermine national solidarity.
witty_quote: I cannot draft a clause that demands all the rights of the Union while repudiating all the obligations toward its citizens!

quiz.question: Why did Dr. Ambedkar refuse to draft Article 370 for Jammu & Kashmir?
options: He was too busy drafting other articles
He refused to endorse a one-sided provision that demanded Indian defense and funding while denying equal rights to Indian citizens in Kashmir
quiz.hint: Ambedkar firmly believed in equal rights and reciprocity for all Indian citizens across every state.
